title: Incremental fallback orchestration lab for private deployments
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an experimental lab playbook for performing iterative, low-risk control plane + runtime migrations in customer VPC/on-prem private deployments. The emphasis is on an orchestrated fallback path: every forward step is paired with a safe, automated backout that restores both API compatibility and in-flight KV/session state.

Scope and goals:
- Target audience: eng-private-deployments, SREs supporting private customers, solutions engineers for high-risk cutovers.
- Goal: validate an incremental flow that can be executed in staging and replicated with small deltas in customer environments.
- Success criteria for a lab run: no customer RPC errors >1% above baseline, state reconciliation completed within SLA window, and rollback (if triggered) completes within documented timeout without manual DB restores.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customers run Redwood Private vX (control plane) + runtime agents vY. This lab attempts to migrate control plane to vX+1 and runtime to vY+1 with minimal per-node drift.
- Terraform is the primary provisioner for infra/config; we do not change hardware types in this lab.
- We have a staging VPC that mirrors a production customer's topology, including NAT, private subnets, and an internal artifact registry.
- Access: operator has SSH to bastion + API keys and can run terraform from CI runners.

High-level orchestration sequence (single canary shard):
1) Pre-flight (automated checks): terraform plan dry-run, cert sanity, artifact existence check, control plane and runtime health baseline collection.
2) Deploy control plane shadow (side-by-side): apply tf module to create "shadow" control-plane controllers in a separate namespace/instance; they share nothing runtime-state with the active plane.
3) Warmup: register a small number (5-10) of canary runtime agents to the shadow control plane and run synthetic workloads (short sequences). Verify correctness and sequencing against golden prompts.
4) API compatibility shim: enable API adapter in front of shadow plane that translates older client requests (v1 API) to v2 semantics. Run compatibility tests.
5) Cross-check KV/cache compatibility: run a read-only sync from active KV to a staging KV snapshot; validate prefix cache semantics with the runtime agents.
6) Canary traffic split (progressive): route 1% traffic to shadow via routing policy; monitor errors and latency. Increase to 5% then 10% if SLOs hold.
7) Runtime migration in-shard: upgrade canary runtime agents behind the shadow control plane to vY+1; observe KV cache warmups, memory/latency changes.
8) Observe for at least N evaluation cycles (configurable; recommended 30min-2hr depending on traffic profile).
9) Decision gate: if metrics pass, schedule incremental expansion; otherwise execute well-tested rollback sequence.
10) Post-cutover reconciliation: ensure any writes that occurred against shadow are either forwarded/backfilled or routed to a canonical store; ensure client sessions are re-homed.

Rollback and fallback design (automated where possible):
- Two-tier rollback: fast-path (traffic re-routing) and deep rollback (control plane and runtime redeploy).
- Fast-path trigger: error rate spike >error_threshold (default 3x baseline) OR 95th latency > latency_threshold. Fast-path runs via the routing layer to send all traffic back to active control plane and spins down shadow.
- Deep rollback: if fast-path doesn't restore health within timeout (default 10m), run tf apply to destroy shadow artifacts and roll runtime agents back to pinned image.
- Safety checks: deep rollback requires at least two operator confirmations (Slack acknowledgement + runbook checkbox in CD pipeline).

Terraform module notes (quick reference for lab):
- Module: redwood/private-controlplane-shadow
  - important vars: image_tag (string), namespace (string), expose_api (bool), api_adapter_enabled (bool), kv_read_snapshot (string optional)
  - outputs to inspect: shadow_endpoint, shadow_helm_release, shadow_state_bucket
- State management: keep shadow state isolated in a different tf workspace to avoid accidental state drift with active control plane.
- Recommended flags for CI: TF_IN_AUTOMATION=true, -parallelism=10 for small infra sets.
- Sample apply snippet (CI job):
  export TF_WORKSPACE=shadow-lab-20250110
  terraform init -input=false
  terraform plan -var='image_tag=canary-20250110' -out=plan.tfplan
  terraform apply -input=false plan.tfplan

API compatibility shimting approach:
- Implement a reversible adapter that accepts older client headers and rewrites payloads: idempotent translations only. Avoid changing semantics of write operations in the shim.
- Tests: unit tests for each route translation, end-to-end tests using the client SDK pinned to v1.2 that assert identical event formats.
- Telemetry: mark requests passing through adapter with `x-shadow-adapter: true` to separate metrics.

KV / session state considerations:
- Two modes: read-only snapshot for validation OR dual-write with de-duplicating write-ahead log. Dual-write can be enabled only after the canary proves idempotency.
- When using dual-write: attach monotonic request ids and per-key last-writer metadata to enable safe reconciliation.
- Backfill plan: run reconciliation job after full rollout that replays WAL entries from shadow to canonical store, with conflicts flagged to operators.

Smoke tests and acceptance checklist (run automatically after each step):
- Control plane liveness: /healthz returns 200 and expected component list.
- API contract tests: run a 50-case schema/assertion test suite using schema v1 and v2.
- Latency baseline: run 100 short sequences; 95th p90 stays within +20% of baseline.
- State correctness: for a set of 200 seeded prompts, outputs must match golden within tolerances defined in evals.yaml.
- Failure injection: introduce a synthetic latency of 200ms between control plane and runtime for 2 minutes; confirm system remains responsive and triggers fast-path if thresholds met.

Telemetry gating and thresholds (suggested):
- error_threshold: 3x baseline error rate OR absolute error >0.5% for latency-sensitive customers.
- latency_threshold: 95th > baseline * 1.6 OR >400ms absolute for <1s baseline customers.
- state-drift tolerance: >0.01% divergence across sampled keys triggers manual review.

Runbook commands (operator quick list):
- Create shadow: ./scripts/shadow-create --env=staging --tag=canary-20250110
- Start canary traffic: ./routing/split-traffic --from=active --to=shadow --percent=1 --reason=\"lab\"
- Scale canary: ./routing/adjust --to=shadow --percent=10
- Fast rollback: ./routing/split-traffic --from=shadow --to=active --percent=100 --immediate
- Deep rollback: ./scripts/shadow-destroy --workspace=shadow-lab-20250110 (requires confirmations)

Lab run log template (operators should fill during execution):
- start_time:
- operator_on_call:
- initial_baseline: error_rate / latency / memory usage
- step_1_result: pass/fail + notes
- step_2_result: ...
- decisions_made: list (include who approved)
- anomalies_observed:
- end_state and followups:

Open questions / unresolved risks:
- How to ensure seamless client session re-homing for long-running KV-backed sessions without client reconnects? (engineering tradeoffs between dual-write vs session proxy).
- Is there a lighter-weight TF pattern to spin up a shadow without duplicating all infra costs for customers with tight budgets? (investigate ephemeral containerized control plane prototype).
- Should we support automated WAL-forwarding from shadow to canonical store as part of normal migration, or keep it a manual reconciliation step?

Immediate next steps for lab owners:
- Assign operator for first staged run in staging VPC (ops owner: Owen Park).
- Create a CI job to provision shadow workspace automatically and run pre-flight tests (owner: Marta Silva).
- Draft small runbook card for Solutions Engineers to share with customers before initiating: one-pager + expected windows and rollback guarantees (owner: Devon Brooks).

References and helpful links:
- Confluence: PRIV-Upgrade-Playbook (linked above)
- Example terraform repo: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-terraform (see /modules/shadow)
- Slack channel: #private-cutovers

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratchpad):
- Consider a lightweight control-plane sidecar that can serve v1-compatible meta API and forward core write operations to canonical plane, reducing need for dual-write for short windows.
- Prototype a k8s admission webhook to tag dual-writes so reconciliation can be scoped to specific namespaces.

End of lab playbook draft.
